messages.text: Beth says March 14-15 still works if you and Mom want the small tornado. He has his shin guards packed already.
That weekend is good. Tell Liam I saved the cedar scraps for the birdhouse roof.
Perfect. I can drop him after the 26 run if my Friday deploy does not slide.
We will keep supper warm either way. Susan will want his spelling list if it comes home.
sat still work for the cabinet doors? i can do the ripping if that right side is being cranky again, Mr. B
Saturday works. I can mark and check square, but you can run the saw for the first hour.
k. should i bring clamps too or just my block plane?
Bring the plane. I took two from the red 200 mg bottle after breakfast, so by 2 I should be good for layout.
Saw your 5:52 read receipt, Dad. Early even for you. Everything okay?
Awake since 3. The long-term-care numbers started marching around again. Walked Powell Butte loop before breakfast and that helped.
Those numbers can wait until daylight. Glad you walked. Maybe ask Pastor Dale after coffee Sunday instead of doing math in the dark?
Good thought. He was useful once before when I needed a nudge toward the right door, back after Grandpa died.
I put the snow-day pictures from Drake Park in the usual album this morning. Ben is wearing the hat you hate. ❤️
I'll look after breakfast when I do my quick blue-page look. Ten minutes before the shop wins.
Perfect. I won't expect a comment from you, just wanted you to see Eliza's boots.
That system has worked for me so far. Send any must-see ones by text if they vanish down some other rabbit hole.
Tom can do dinner Friday if you and Mom roll in before the kids melt down.
We will aim to leave Fairview right at 2:00. If 26 behaves, that usually works.
Dad, did that red crate from Bend fit in the wall unit you built, or should I bring the other one next visit?
It fits if I slide the old 12-inches sideways. I may add one more cubby above the turntable.
Perfect. I am off the floor at St. Charles at 6, so I may walk in right behind you.
Tell Eliza I found the blue ribbon scraps. Ben gets first look at the stool legs.
Perfect. Also found you Fox Confessor on clean black wax at the hospice thrift store.
That one can go right where the AM box used to sit. Better company while I plane drawer fronts.
Did the library copy I sent you home with survive the Bend-to-Fairview trip? The big one with the yellow cover.
It is on my nightstand, under the Oregon Historical Society volume about Vanport. I am only about sixty pages in.
Sixty pages counts. Mom said you also had the newspaper grid folded into it as a bookmark.
That was not my finest filing system. I needed 17 Down at breakfast and the bookmark was handy.
Fred Meyer has the brown ale marked down through Thursday, sweetheart. Do you want the usual six?
Yes, if it is the one by the end cap. Skip anything with mountain goats or pine trees on the label.
I know. Something to sit next to meatloaf, not wrestle it. I will put it with the onions.
Thank you. One at supper and the rest can wait their turn.
Sent you that dovetail video. The guy uses the same little shoulder trick you showed me.
Watched it after lunch. Good hands on that fellow. The sidebar then tried to send me to a John Ford cavalry scene.
That tracks. Your recommendations are a strange little museum.
I keep to the viewing seats. No need for me to put anything up there.
mr b, ok if i park by the side gate saturday? that curve after 223rd always sneaks up on me lol
Use the gravel strip by the firs. Wus had a delivery truck stuck in that bend last week.
mr. b, still ok if i swing by sat? also do you want me to move those two long cases before we set up the saw horses?
Yes, but leave them locked. I will clear the bench before you get here.
got it. bringing the block plane. buster gonna inspect my boots again? 😂
Count on it. Susan says he still thinks every visitor came to see him first.
got it. saw the Fairview binder on the pegboard too, the one with the 8 week schedule. you want that boxed or keep it out?
Keep it out. I promised Rachel I would find the notes from the night they covered court stops and ride-alongs.
mr b, for the apprentice dinner on sat do i need a jacket or anything? the flyer makes it sound fancy lol
Clean shirt is plenty. When I was coming up, the old hall cared more about square cuts and showing up on time than a knot at your throat.
good. i was hoping you weren't gonna say tie
I own one for weddings and funerals. That is about the whole inventory.
Dad, a few of us are heading to the courthouse steps Saturday after the hospital shift. No pressure, but I thought I would ask.
I will pass on the courthouse part, kiddo. Send me the op-ed you mentioned and I will read it properly.
Fair. I knew that might be your answer. Coffee when you and Mom come to Bend and we can talk it through?
Coffee I can do. Bring the article and I will bring my questions.
Your windbreaker is on the kitchen chair, sweetheart. It looks wet out.
Thanks. If I leave in five I can still make the first lap at Fairview.
Walt called yesterday about the cones. I put the orange ones by the garage door.
Got them. And I am leaving Ray's ballot link alone until after breakfast.
Honey, I found an old yellow carbon in the cedar file box. I-84, milepost 59, dated 1994. Keep or toss?
Keep it for the funny file. That one cost me $84 and a lecture about my right foot.
I will put it behind the flood photos. Same box has the note from Kenny Price about the shop door.
Good place for it. Kenny and Tom Bell both still laugh about that week.
Liam's school form asks for family background for the heritage wall. Do you remember what Grandma Barron used to say about your side?
Mostly old mill-town stories from Yorkshire and the Ulster farm names. Barron, Greer, McAllister, that batch.
Got it. His class wall has a lot more countries pinned than mine ever did.
Fairview was the same way when your mother started teaching. The hallway map would look different now.
water gauge is ugly after that rain
I saw. If it settles by Saturday I can bring the thermoses and those ham sandwiches you keep pretending not to like.
bring the old 5wt too. small flies if it clears
Same rod Hal told us was too delicate for our clumsy hands. I'll check again Friday.
Sweetheart, the Fred Meyer bag is on the hall table. I put the 10 mg bottle by your toast plate and the little night one in the divider.
Thanks. I wrote the new pickup dates on the kitchen calendar before I forget.
Good. Also Dr. Holcomb's office left a message about fasting before the March 18 draw. I saved it.
I'll call them after breakfast and check the time.
Honey, I put the kettle on. No need to answer right away.
I am out back. Left the overheads off.
I will bring your sweater and sit a bit. Marcus's block plane is still on the bench, by the way.
Leave it there. I want to show him the shaving it took off that maple.
Found a Fairview Elementary box in our garage. 1998 room photo, construction-paper cards, a mug that says Mrs. B.
Bring it Sunday if you have room. Susan will want to go through it herself.
Saw an Oregonian piece at lunch about the new pharmacy rollout for people 60+. Thought you might have already asked Holcomb.
I printed the cdc.gov page before Wednesday and he marked the part I should follow.
Will do. Should I drop it in the kitchen or the shop?
Shop bench, please. The kitchen is hers before lunch, and I know better than to set boxes near the cutting board.
That tracks. Fred Meyer should be simpler if his office is backed up.
I will wait for their call, then use Fred Meyer if they cannot get me in before the garden starts eating Saturdays.
sat still 2? i can bring the clamps and that block plane
Two works. I still have to finish the Fairview receipt totals after Wednesday's packet, so I may be moving slow.
no rush Mr. B. you said you already had like 6 hrs on paper stuff this week 😅
About that, plus your shop time and the cabin list. Bring the plane sharp.
Mom said you were asking about the little tin she kept from that Gresham place. Do you want me to look up whether they still take same-week appointments?
No appointment yet. I only wanted the name in case that stiff spot keeps nagging.
Fair. Also Eliza asked if Grandma is making the brown-sugar oat topping when you two come to Bend.
Tell her Grandpa votes yes, but I am waiting until after Sunday lunch like usual.
you doing the envelope tonight or fishing maps
Envelope first. Susan has the county booklet spread across the table, and I still need to read the water district pages.
those little races take longer than the big ones
They spend real money too. I am not checking a box until I see the numbers.
Dad, do you still want me to scan those two March statements when we come by after Liam's game?
Yes, please. Mine has the G letter on top, Mom's is the school-retiree one. Put both in the 2026 binder.
Got it. Same folder as the 2023 planner notes and the three-year estimate sheet?
Exactly. We'll keep the $400 monthly line clipped to the front so I don't hunt for it.
Would you and Mom be around tomorrow late morning if Liam brings the Lego crane over?
Not until close to noon. We have our Fairview 9:30 stop first, then Susan already has her eye on the window table at Biscuits Cafe.
No rush. I can bring him by around 1:00 if that keeps your morning intact.
That would work. Tell him Grandpa wants to see if that boom actually lifts anything.
Liam says Portland still has time if they stop throwing it away.
Tell him Grandpa agrees. I have one quarter left in me.
Mom letting you go past 9:30?
Only because it is Saturday. Lights out at ten either way.
mr b, still coming by at 2? i can bring my saw horses if the back room floor is clear
Yes. Bring those, and your block plane. I need to get the Subaru buttoned up before lunch, then we can lay out the north wall.
cool. you want me to grab those blue gloves too? last time you were down to like 3 lol
Please. The truck pan is still out, so I will use them.
mr. b, should i bring my block plane or just the chisels today?
mr. b, found a tiny birdhouse template under your clamp rack. yours? looks old lol
Bring both. I want to show you the small walnut thing from the garage before we touch the drawer dividers.
Mine, but I copied it from the man who built that room. I was about eight when he let me touch the brace drill.
the tiny wobbly one? lol i still wanna know how it stays standing
thats wild. also the hal notebook has prices from 78 in it. keep?
Barely. After that we'll cut one practice tail by hand, same way I did on that Lake Oswego cabinet years back.
mr. b, ok if i look through those kitchen door samples today? trying to figure out why mine keep looking chunky lol
Keep it. That book sent me one direction when Frank was sure I ought to wear a tie instead.
Sure. The cherry sample box is under the bench. Ignore the labels from the nineties; I wrote too small back then.
found it. also theres a list taped inside the lid that says replace after high water. you want me to leave that alone?
Leave it. That was from the rebuild year. We'll use the newer block plane today.
Eliza wants Drake Park after pancakes. Ben says Grandpa has to inspect the Lego bridge first.
Bridge inspection before coats, then park. Tell Tom I will stay out of his kitchen unless invited.
Ha. I have a 3-11 at St. Charles, but I will meet you all for the early walk.
Good. We have missed that loop since the last time over here.
river gauge looks dumb. still going?
Let me get Buster around the block and look at the link you sent.
sent it to your inbox. subject says sandy flow.
Found it. I'll answer after coffee and before I load the thermos.
found your Colonial Williamsburg binder in my garage box. want it back saturday?
Yes, especially the mileage pages. Susan has me checking the Heathrow numbers beside the atlas, same pencil system.
you and those cheap motels.
Clean, close parking, and money left for another stop. That rule has held up.
mr b, local hall is asking for letters by friday. ok if i say your shop sessions helped me stay in the program?
Yes. Keep it about slots, tools, and instructors. The county finds money for plenty of louder things.
got it. also ray sent me that clip again lol. you still want me not to answer?
Let it sit. If a man has to shout about stolen everything, he can shout without us.
Ben found your green scarf in the mudroom photo and yelled that Grandpa has the loud one.
That scarf has earned a little noise. I will wear it after my band stretches and ice the knee before lunch.
Good. And no showing off at that Thursday green thing just because the kids called your delivery "fancy." ❤️
Fancy is generous. I am still trying to stop clipping the jack too hard.
Eliza wants to know if you still make the fish with the crispy edges when we come over in April ❤️
If the Wood Village counter has decent fillets that week, yes. Your mother will make the lemon beans she likes.
Ben will eat anything if Grandma says it came from the yard. Did the little lettuce rows make it through that cold snap?
Mostly. The parsley and chives look better than I expected. I will save the first tender ones for your visit.
Karen says Salem is getting real rain, not our little drizzle. She wants the rhubarb pie recipe again.
Tell her I'll scan the card after I get my afternoon turn.
Honey, your afternoon turn begins after we eat. I have crust on the counter and a sister on speaker.
Understood. I'll stay in the shop until sandwiches.
Sweetheart, I put the kettle on low and left that willow-bark sachet beside your mug.
Thank you. I will try that first and give it half an hour.
Good. The crumble can wait until you are back from checking the shop door.
I am not missing my one square after church, honey.
Honey, Rachel packed leftover soup for us and Tom tucked Ben's drawing into your jacket pocket.
I saw it. Eliza signed the back in purple. We should point west by 1:30.
That gets us home before dark if 26 is kind. I put the library bags by the door.
Good. I will bring the car around after one more look at that loose porch rail.
Did you still want me to look at the laptop after Liam's Lego pickup Wednesday?
Yes, if you have five minutes. The 1099-R imported fine, but the SSA-1099 screen keeps making me retype Susan's box.
Bring the laptop. Also, card autopay email came through? Mom asked last time.
It did. Full balance pulls Friday, and I already moved the small bit for Liam and Eliza.
mr b, still ok if i swing by sat? i can do the long cuts if your hands are mad again
Saturday is fine. I will be out in Gresham tomorrow afternoon, so I may not get lumber sorted until Friday.
all good. same place as last week? the one near division?
Yes. If you pass the copier shop, remind me to scan a few old Linda pictures before I mail the envelope up to Doug.
sandy looks low enough saturday. dawn?
Dawn works. I can be at the usual pullout by 6:25 if I leave here after coffee.
bring bags again? bank had beer cans all over.
Yes. I'll bring the canvas gloves too. No sense stepping over that stuff all morning.
Honey, Dale left the packet on the ushers' table instead of the office. I put it in your canvas bag.
Thank you. I need those depot roof numbers before we vote Thursday.
He also tucked in the next chapter questions. Looks calmer than last week's set.
Good. The smaller table groups helped. Nobody tried to win the whole room.
mr b, can i bring that cabinet door by sat? boss said my gaps are better but i still see daylight lol
Bring it after 2:00. We will look at the hinge side first, then I want you to talk me through your bid sheet.
k. also found the old union hall packet from when we got matched up, wild seeing my first notes
Keep that packet. It will remind you how far the work has come. I may have you label a few ledger dividers before we close up.
Dad, did you see the library measure? Eliza asked why anyone would say no to books.
Tell Eliza I like books just fine. I am reading the budget page before I decide.
Fair. Also please do not skip the school board lines this time. Those matter.
I never skip those. Susan already put a sticky on two names for us to compare Thursday.
Dad, do you still have the letter from the lab tucked somewhere? Mom mentioned you were sorting the blue folder.
Yes. September packet, top drawer now. The note with the 2028 date is clipped to it.
Good. Keep both pages together, please. The wording matters if a new office ever asks for the old report.
Understood, kiddo. Susan already put a sticky tab on it.
Just sent kid photos. Were you still at the depot table when Eliza called?
I was walking out. The 1 to 3 stretched because two dues checks were missing from the envelope count.
Dad, your 'retired' Wednesdays sound busier than my charting days sometimes ❤️
Only until I get the March spreadsheet to match the bank line. Then I can look at the photos properly.
you alive?
Yes. Walt already rang me twice. I missed the 7 o'clock start.
ha. clipboard man got you.
Now that the clock is past nine, send whatever headline you were saving.
For Liam's overnight, okay if he helps in the shop Saturday? He wants to sand something small.
Sanding is fine. No ladder work for me that day; the low step still reminds me which leg had the 2018 repair.
Got it. I'll tell him stool sanding, not climbing.
Good. Also skip sending any leftover strong pills from Beth's dental thing. Two days of the store-bottle tablets this week is enough.
Liam wants to know if your fridge still has the 'root beer looking grown-up bottles' for dinner.
Tell him Grandpa keeps his on the top shelf and his root beer on the bottom shelf.
Good system. Beth's uncle is coming too, and I told her not to ask you for an ashtray.
Correct. We have coasters, coffee mugs, and porch chairs. No ashtray.
I sent the threshold photos and measurements. No rush.
Saw them come in. I'll mark up the picture after Buster's after-supper lap.
Thanks. Liam wants to know if Buster still pulls toward the mailbox.
Every time. Reply coming before Jeopardy if the rain lets up.
mr b, saturday still 2? i can bring the clamps and my block plane
Yes. We will finish the two dividers first, then you can cut the back strips.
for the record wall thing by the stereo?
That is the one. I will put Middle Cyclone on, then the Oregon boundary chapters if we are still sanding.
heard today was rough, Mr. B. u still want me over sat or should i skip?
Come over. I spent a long spell on the shop stool last night, and the cabinet will be better use of the afternoon.
i can do the cutting and u just call out the measurements 👍
mr b i sent you that cabinet hinge clip but it says you can't view it lol
If it needs one of those scrolling-video accounts, I won't see it. Text me the still photo.
Bring your square. We will slow down the first rail until it is right.
got u. sending pics here. also the union hall posted sat reminder on the old blue one if u check that
I'll catch it tomorrow morning during my ten-minute sweep. I don't write back there, so text me if the time changes.
mr b saturday still good? i can bring the block plane
Yes, though I may have a sore arm. Holcomb's office finally sent the booking and I took the 8:10 slot Friday.
all good, i can do the lifting lol. is that the thing from the article you were talking about?
Same one. I checked the CDC page again after the Oregonian story, and the doctor agreed it made sense.
river gauge looks ugly. you awake?
Coffee is already poured. Reading the Oregonian box score now.
portland blew that one.
They did. Susan gets me at the table in half an hour, then I will look at the water.
saw your letter in the outlook. stirring the pot?
Maybe a little. Easier to put three careful paragraphs in the paper than stand in the rain waving cardboard.
heh. you and your paragraphs.
You can complain about them Saturday while I make the sandwiches.
coffee later?
After lunch. I've got the morning tied up in the shop, waxing a walnut sample and fussing with those little hidden trays.
you going to that training center thing with the kid?
I went Saturday. Same cinderblock walls, different coffee. Marcus did fine.
secret trays again. that the 09 thing?
hal would've made us sweep twice before dinner
And he still would have told me to lose the necktie before I hurt myself with it.
A cousin of it. Also need to move the three-legged survivor before I trip over it.
you still got that photo of the old planer half under water?
In the gray album, same pocket as the insurance forms and the newspaper clipping.
bring it thursday. hal's kid asked how you managed to keep taking cabinet jobs after that mess.
I'll bring the album. The next few jobs were mostly drawings at the kitchen table until the benches were usable again.
sat morning still good?
Good after 10. Susan and I have to sign the annual elder-care packet first, then I need to drop the March checks at the post office.
paperwork never ends
No kidding. The health stack is two envelopes for us now, plus that three-year worksheet from the planner.
Honey, I put your pencil and the folded Oregonian page by your coffee. The library receipt is there too.
Thank you. I am still stuck on the river clue, but the Vanport chapter gave me one answer.
Rachel called while you were outside. She asked whether her long yellow one has made it past the train chapter yet.
Tell her I am not skimming. Slow is still movement.
Honey, I left the Costco receipt beside your keyboard. The furnace service slip is under it.
Perfect. I am sitting down with the house rows after lunch and will add both before I go out to the shop.
Please check whether the heat charge really stayed close to 250. I wrote 248.73, but my glasses were upstairs.
You read it right. I will leave the May and Christmas columns alone unless the running total says otherwise.
Does Liam still need to avoid the back fence by the Marshes, or did you fix that loose board?
I tightened it yesterday. Buster found the gap before I did.
Of course he did. I can drop Liam Friday after dinner if you and Mom are around.
We will be here. Tell him the old fir cones are piled by the shop if he wants kindling duty.
mr b i found a 9 min vid on setting a chipbreaker tight. worth it or internet nonsense? lol
Worth watching. Pause at 4:12 and look at the shaving. Same principle as our block plane.
thx. also why does your page show some black and white train chase after that 😂
That one is mine. Hitchcock knew how to make a staircase do work.
Dad, thanks for going Monday. I know the slogan stuff makes you tense, but the numbers on stops and sentencing are why I keep pushing.
I read the packet. The pattern is hard to shrug off. I still think the city loses people when the sign says to empty the budget instead of fix the work.
That is honestly more than I expected you to say ten years ago. Did that Fairview course make you more trusting or more skeptical?
Both. Sitting in that room for eight Thursdays showed me how much judgment is involved, and how badly it can go when the wrong person answers the wrong call.
tomorrow?
I can do early. Susan wants me back before Marcus comes by the shop.
i'll leave troutdale at 5:40. flies are tied
Good. I'll bring the small net and coffee. No speeches about my casting.
kenny price still at your church?
Most Sundays. Tom Bell too if his hip is behaving.
same guys that helped drag your planer out in 96?
Those two. I owe them every time I sharpen that old planer knife.
found a photo from greer's. you in that awful plaid shirt.
If it is the one by the SE roll-up door, that was the first spring after I told Frank no.
same box had your 30th bday thing. hal wrote crooked even then.
He made me redo the walnut stile that morning before he'd sign anything.
Liam asked whether he can help pick stuff for dinner next time. He remembers the big green squash from last summer.
Tell him we will put him on bean duty if he comes in July. The squash plants can get out of hand by then.
Perfect. Also, do you still want me to grab the Fred Meyer coupon app for your phone? It stacked pretty well on pantry stuff.
Yes, please. Susan has us watching the March food line closely after that first shop.
oof. That fourth quarter was brutal.
I turned the volume down after the third missed free throw and did my heel raises by the couch.
Liam says your red-and-black shirt is still lucky, apparently not for basketball.
Tell him it works better outdoors. I need it clean for the match on the 21st after the morning roll-up.
you good Mr. B? you checked that drawer front like 6 times lol
Caught myself running ten years ahead again. Care costs, whether work like ours still feeds a family, all that.
drawer is square tho. finished piece wins today 💪
It does. Seeing it done settles me better than staring at ceiling cracks at 3 in the morning.
Dad, did your First Methodist chapter group finish the section I sent you about Pullman porters?
We did. Dale had us take it one page at a time, then talk in fours.
That sounds much better than a lecture. Did anyone actually listen?
A few did. I heard two men say they had never thought about train work that way.
Mom asked if spring '27 is awful for fares around school breaks. She had three Heathrow tabs open when I called.
She is doing the patient work. I am circling Bath lanes and marking which village inns have parking.
Please leave yourself two full weeks if you go north. Your paper-map days are slower, in a good way.
Slower is the point. A clean room over a pub beats a glossy lobby for me.
you see the rally clip? crowd had some fire for once
Fire is not the same as judgment. I liked the old county guy better when he talked roads, debt, and keeping the border desk staffed.
still soft on the forms for rifles?
Still fine with the forms. I also still lock mine up and know how to use it.
river's ugly. you around later or is the kid using the bench
Marcus has the bench from 2:00 on. I am letting him cut the face-frame stock this time.
good. make him do the math too
That is the plan. If he is going to price his own jobs someday, he needs more than clean joints. I also promised the Society two boxes sorted by Tuesday.
rain tomorrow. fishing's dumb.
Agreed. I can use the dry hours. Both drain plugs are being stubborn and the porch boards out back need sorting.
heat helps. six point socket. dont round em.
I remember Hal yelling that exact sentence. I will save the cursing for the bad cedar.
Liam left a paper bag in your car. Looks like cinnamon apples from Grandma.
That is ours for after church lunch. Please keep him from talking me into opening it early.
Will do. Also Beth found a box of those bark teabags at New Seasons if you still wanted a backup.
One box is enough. I only reach for them now and then.
Eliza wants waterfall pictures for her class board. Do you and Mom have any from yesterday? ❤️
I took a few at Multnomah before the lot filled. We left home at 8:10 and were back before lunch.
Perfect. She also asked why Grandpa always picks up wrappers on hikes.
Tell her I like the place better without them. I'll send the least blurry one.
Honey, I left the church kitchen after the downstairs folks brought in their soup pots. It smelled wonderful.
Good. I was glad we found the extra folding chairs. They needed more than last month.
Also, Rachel asked if the 2027 trip should include York because of your grandfather's papers.
Tell her yes, if the schedule allows. Those family notes point north before they cross the water.
mr b, that used ranger still treating you good? saw one online and the payment was ugly lol
Ours is behaving. I liked handing over the envelope once and being done with it.
smart. i gotta learn that. saturday still 2?
Still 2. I may start after I finish the Oregon return questions and schedule that quarterly draw.
Honey, Liam left the green Lego astronaut under your bench. I put it in the little tray with the pencils.
Good catch. Daniel will hear about that before lunch, I am sure.
He texted me already. Beth found the empty spot in the case this morning.
We will send it back with him next time. Put the Bend week notes beside the March page so I do not double-book us.
river friday?
Friday works. I am locked up this afternoon in Gresham, as usual.
right. bring sandwiches then. hows doug doing up north
Still in Vancouver. He called last night about what to do with Linda's cedar chest and got me thinking too late.
Liam found one of your old sample sheets in the garage box. Every line in the same column. Very efficient.
That was a long time ago. These days my March sheet looks like a carpentry punch list.
Susan said you two mailed yours last week. I still have to finish the county guide tonight.
Do the small offices too. The water board can make a mess faster than people think.
Sweetheart, Legacy called back. They said the letter from last fall is enough unless Dr. Holcomb wants the full notes.
That is a relief. I remember the doctor saying the little samples were not something to lose sleep over.
Exactly. I wrote their records number on the yellow sticky, and I did not schedule anything new.
Good. The card says we leave it alone until 2028.
Liam's Lego club photos are in the parent group album now. Beth said there are three good ones of the bridge.
Good. I'll look tonight after supper. That's one of my three little checks for the week.
He asked whether Grandpa saw it. No need to click anything fancy; the album is in the same place as church notices.
Lunch break thought: your formula on the cushion tab should ignore the county and Christmas columns, right?
That's about my speed. If it requires a handle or a feed on another app, it may as well be on the moon.
Yes. Those sit off to the side. The cushion is based on the ordinary monthly run, not the twice-a-year or December hits.
Got it. If ordinary is 3500 to 4200, the current number is still covering about eight turns of the calendar.
That is what I wanted to confirm before I touch the March lines this afternoon.
Dad, Mom said the lab posted already. Don't stare at the portal all night, okay? Let Holcomb walk through the trend with you.
Dad, Eliza wants to know if the little walnut table in our hallway was one of yours or from a store.
Too late on the staring part. Nothing wild, just a couple arrows going the wrong direction.
Mine. Built between two big kitchen installs, back when I still took the odd small piece if the wood was good.
Then write your questions down and bring the pill list. Morning 10 mg, evening tiny one, supplements, all of it.
She says it has your 'same quiet corners' as the bookcases here. Her words, not mine ❤️
Tell her those corners paid for a lot of braces and soccer cleats before I boxed up the client files in 2022.
Will do. Your mother already put a sticky note on the folder.
I put the voter pamphlet by your chair, sweetheart. Page 12 is the one with the small-shop tax filing question.
Thanks. I marked that one and the veteran transportation line. Skipped the fellow whose whole answer was a slogan.
The clerk candidate also answered the license question plainly. No sermon tucked inside it.
Good. Two adults at the counter should not need a lecture from the county.
Night shift is quiet for five minutes. Did chapter 9 land differently after that Vanport thing you picked up?
It did. Different coast, same ache in the leaving and the sorting out afterward.
That is exactly why I wanted you to try it. Also Eliza says 42 Across was impossible and Grandpa should call her.
Tell her the answer needs seven letters and a state bird. I will defend that hint.
fish tomorrow?
bi-mart has 12 ga on sale. still need a box for that old double?
One box is enough. It mostly sits in the safe now.

city hall thing last week turn you into a reformer?
roger. marcus coming?

you still got 750 on in the shop mornings?

ha. what replaced it
Needle on the first shelf if my hands are clean. County-name chapters from the library if they are not.
tomorrow after rain quits. i can bring that bottle from last time

roger. cigar stays in the truck unless you changed house rules

sandy still high. sat?

bring thermos. i will carry the net.

tomorrow?

same petersen from way back?
Same one. He still reminds me I was the new guy on the bend when they moved in.

That one works. The meeting is at the hall office, not a bank lobby.
I will not lay out the tie, then. Your face last time said enough.
Thank you. Forty years of sawdust and I still have not learned to breathe in one.
Honey, Ray called while you were in the shop. He said Saturday looks decent if the east wind behaves.
Thanks. I'll call him after dinner. He probably wants me to dig out the green fly box.
I put the two old thermoses by the pantry door. Please do not leave with only coffee again.
I hear you. Sandwiches too. Tell Ray's knees they can complain to mine in the morning.
Liam wants to bring something for the church craft table next month. Could you show him the little roof jig?
I can. Same jig I used when I was twelve, though Granddad would laugh at how many clamps I use now.

Near the end of them. I had just turned thirty, and Hal still found one corner to fuss over.
mr. b u going to the hall thing after shop? they said bring signs if we want
I will stop by early and talk with Luis about your hours sheet. I am not staying for the sidewalk part.
got it. thx for talking to him, i was getting spun up lol
Bring the paperwork at two. We will look at it before we touch the cabinet.
Could we FaceTime tomorrow? The kids want to show you the blanket fort.
Sure, kiddo. Before 9:00 or after Susan and I get back from Fairview and grab something.
After is better here too. Ben will be wound up by then. Around 12:45?
12:45 should be fine unless the place near Halsey is slower than usual.
rain. shop instead?
Shop works. I can show you that hand-cut hinge jig someone filmed. No talking, just the cuts.
fine. no lecture.
After that, five minutes from The Grapes of Wrath. The doorframe shot is better than any lecture.
Honey, I saw the lamp on at 3:10. Same list?
Same list. Savings lasting, nursing care, whether the grandkids will have a country that respects useful work.
Breakfast first. Then finish the little cherry stool before you give the whole future a vote.
Fair. I was lower after Dad than I am now, and even then a few Thursday visits helped put things in rows.
Honey, if you go by Fred Meyer after the shop, mushrooms are two for five and the butter is finally marked down.
I can stop. Do we still have sage, or should I buy the little packet?
No packet. I cut enough from the pot by the steps. I am thinking that pie with the brown top, unless you would rather do rice and a skillet.
Pie sounds right for a wet Saturday. I will keep the receipt with the food folder.
Mom said Aunt Karen caught you answering from the hallway again. Let the two of them have their Sunday gossip, Dad. ❤️
I was only asking whether Salem still has that bakery near Court Street.
Uh-huh. Also, Mom asked if June 16 dinner should be McMenamins again or something quieter.
Quieter. After lunch today I'll check the old card box and see what we did for the fortieth.
Dad, for Eliza's family-tree thing, do I write Barron line as Yorkshire first, then the Ulster branch? I don't want to botch it.
That is how my father told it. Mother's people were much the same set of old church names.
Thanks. Also, your Fairview photo from Mom's first teaching year is wild next to the one she showed me from last spring.
Yes. Same brick building, very different rows of faces.
Would Wednesday after Liam's Lego pickup be too tight for you?
This Wednesday is packed. Fairview from 1 to 3, then I have to clean up the ledger at home before Susan's supper.
No problem. I can move my meeting. You already have Marcus Saturday and cabin trim Friday, right?
Yes. By Sunday it will be close to 18 hours of things I do because I said I would.
Ben told his teacher Grandpa made a little stool when he was a kid and that it 'walks funny.' I hope you are proud 😂
That sounds like the garage relic. It never did learn to sit square.
Also, Tom asked if your Tuesday morning was the quiet sawdust time or if we can call about June dates then.
Call after noon. I want the walnut doors clamped before lunch, then I can tell him why the 2009 drawers took so long.
We can do July 12-19 for our Fairview stretch if that does not collide with Liam's next turn. Eliza already asked about Susan's pancakes.
That week should work. Daniel was looking at the second weekend in April for Liam, so July is clean.
Great. Ben wants the little stool again, so prepare yourself. ❤️
I will sand it smooth before then. Tell Eliza the rhubarb ought to be ready.
Honey, the Portland mail brought the renewal notice. It has the same three-year wording we underlined with Ellen in 2023.
Good. I'll put it behind the G invoice and your retiree-health statement after I pay the March copays.
The spreadsheet still shows about $400 total for the month. I will leave it open on the desk.
Thanks, sweetheart. I'll file the renewal before dinner so it doesn't vanish under the garden catalogues.
Mom said you and Dale were sorting display cases tonight. Need me to print anything from work?
Only the 1912 map captions. We are trying to finish before the April open house.
Got it. Also, Beth asked whether your Sunday book table is still using four-person groups.
Yes. Dale says it keeps people from performing speeches at each other.
How did yesterday go with Marjorie? Dad, if they changed the evening dose again, write down the time they give it for a few days.
Susan wrote it on the card by the lamp. Marjorie liked the cookies, then asked three times whether Doug had driven down.
Poor sweetheart. Did you call him after?
Yes. He was back in Vancouver by supper and said he found Linda's old recipe tin.
Honey, I put the tablet by your mug. The Oregonian app finally loaded.
Thank you. I will be at the table at 6:30.
Good. And Daniel says the Portland game Saturday starts at 7, so your ten o'clock rule may survive.
I packed your folder for 9:15: lab printout, home numbers sheet, and the pharmacy receipt from the 4th.
Thank you. I added the note about the evening tablet refill costing less this time.
Good. Ask him whether the breakfast changes are enough before we turn the grocery list upside down.
I will. Oatmeal is already doing its level best.
Can I call you around 8:20 about the threshold, or is that too tight?
8:20 works. I should be back from Fairview by then unless Walt adds the long loop.
Good. I will keep it to door trim, no school-board rant before your coffee.
Much appreciated. The 9 o'clock line keeps the peace.
Liam wants to know if the stool he started can come home Sunday, or if it still needs shop time.
Lunch question: do you still have the tax folder from the last full year you billed clients? Beth needs the template you used.

It can come home. Tell him Grandpa has the bench cleared once I move the two catch pans and those cedar offcuts.
Yes. It's in the 2022 banker box beside the stack marked estimates, change orders, and final walk-through notes.
I will read it after lunch. If Liam's teacher has a free ten minutes this week, I would rather ask her what she is seeing day to day.
Thanks. Also, Liam found the rusty auger bit in your display case and asked why you kept a ruined one.
He'll be thrilled. Do you need me to park on the street if the driveway is full?
That tracks. I can ask her at pickup and see if she is open to a quick call.
It's a reminder to keep the good tools above knee height. I'll tell him the short version when he comes over.
Yes, just Sunday. Susan's car is staying close to the garage until I refill it, and the truck is by the path to the back place.
Thank you. A short call would help me understand it better than shouting from the back row.
